2.web: “Truly I know that it is so, but how can man be just with God?
2.asv: Of a truth I know that it is so: But how can man be just with God?

3.web: If he is pleased to contend with him, he can’t answer him one time in a thousand.
3.asv: If he be pleased to contend with him, He cannot answer him one of a thousand.

4.web: God who is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who has hardened himself against him, and prospered?
4.asv: He iswise in heart, and mighty in strength: Who hath hardened himself against him, and prospered?—

5.web: He removes the mountains, and they don’t know it, when he overturns them in his anger.
5.asv: Himthat removeth the mountains, and they know it not, When he overturneth them in his anger;

6.web: He shakes the earth out of its place. Its pillars tremble.
6.asv: That shaketh the earth out of its place, And the pillars thereof tremble;

7.web: He commands the sun, and it doesn’t rise, and seals up the stars.
7.asv: That commandeth the sun, and it riseth not, And sealeth up the stars;

8.web: He alone stretches out the heavens, and treads on the waves of the sea.
8.asv: That alone stretcheth out the heavens, And treadeth upon the waves of the sea;

9.web: He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the rooms of the south.
9.asv: That maketh the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, And the chambers of the south;

10.web: He does great things past finding out; yes, marvelous things without number.
10.asv: That doeth great things past finding out, Yea, marvellous things without number.

11.web: Behold, he goes by me, and I don’t see him. He passes on also, but I don’t perceive him.
11.asv: Lo, he goeth by me, and I see him not: He passeth on also, but I perceive him not.

12.web: Behold, he snatches away. Who can hinder him? Who will ask him, ‘What are you doing?’
12.asv: Behold, he seizeth the prey, who can hinder him? Who will say unto him, What doest thou?

13.web: “God will not withdraw his anger. The helpers of Rahab stoop under him.
13.asv: God will not withdraw his anger; The helpers of Rahab do stoop under him.

14.web: How much less shall I answer him, And choose my words to argue with him?
14.asv: How much less shall I answer him, And choose out my words to reason with him?

15.web: Though I were righteous, yet I wouldn’t answer him. I would make supplication to my judge.
15.asv: Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer; I would make supplication to my judge.

16.web: If I had called, and he had answered me, yet I wouldn’t believe that he listened to my voice.
16.asv: If I had called, and he had answered me, Yet would I not believe that he hearkened unto my voice.

17.web: For he breaks me with a storm, and multiplies my wounds without cause.
17.asv: For he breaketh me with a tempest, And multiplieth my wounds without cause.

18.web: He will not allow me to catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.
18.asv: He will not suffer me to take my breath, But filleth me with bitterness.

19.web: If it is a matter of strength, behold, he is mighty! If of justice, ‘Who,’ says he, ‘will summon me?’
19.asv: Ifwe speakof strength, lo, he ismighty! And if of justice, Who, saith he, will summon me?

20.web: Though I am righteous, my own mouth shall condemn me. Though I am blameless, it shall prove me perverse.
20.asv: Though I be righteous, mine own mouth shall condemn me: Though I be perfect, it shall prove me perverse.

21.web: I am blameless. I don’t respect myself. I despise my life.
21.asv: I am perfect; I regard not myself; I despise my life.

22.web: “It is all the same. Therefore I say he destroys the blameless and the wicked.
22.asv: It is all one; therefore I say, He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked.

23.web: If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.
23.asv: If the scourge slay suddenly, He will mock at the trial of the innocent.

24.web: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He covers the faces of its judges. If not he, then who is it?
24.asv: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He covereth the faces of the judges thereof: Ifit benothe, who then is it?

25.web: “Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away, they see no good,
25.asv: Now my days are swifter than a post: They flee away, they see no good.

26.web: They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey.
26.asv: They are passed away as the swift ships; As the eagle that swoopeth on the prey.

27.web: If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and cheer up;’
27.asv: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad countenance, and be of good cheer;

28.web: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that you will not hold me innocent.
28.asv: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that thou wilt not hold me innocent.

29.web: I shall be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?
29.asv: I shall be condemned; Why then do I labor in vain?

30.web: If I wash myself with snow, and cleanse my hands with lye,
30.asv: If I wash myself with snow water, And make my hands never so clean;

31.web: yet you will plunge me in the ditch. My own clothes shall abhor me.
31.asv: Yet wilt thou plunge me in the ditch, And mine own clothes shall abhor me.

32.web: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, that we should come together in judgment.
32.asv: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, That we should come together in judgment.

33.web: There is no umpire between us, that might lay his hand on us both.
33.asv: There is no umpire betwixt us, That might lay his hand upon us both.

34.web: Let him take his rod away from me. Let his terror not make me afraid;
34.asv: Let him take his rod away from me, And let not his terror make me afraid:

35.web: then I would speak, and not fear him, for I am not so in myself.
35.asv: Then would I speak, and not fear him; For I am not so in myself.
